approval.body: Authorize rule official-aip-stable-physical-identity@0.1.0-draft policy-sha256:7eadcab59d93a2f33c9e9237ad2dc2e258e129f4995bbf60cba35c26d6fe65ae scope-sha256:597ddbc5afeb66df29bf7dcb405846e9ac912ae4bfa93bfd2b71c24a6c8b4e65 executor-sha256:ad99fa4f9fe58b94b3fcc2c584d510df2471f716e6add8277ea6a433d27efd42. Permit automatic physical-site UUID allocation for all future qualifying low-risk airports in this country/issuer scope, without per-airport approval. Require original replay, independent operator site/address evidence, complete edition and competition checks. No code/name validity, relocation, correction, test authority, or direct main writes. Candidate PR only; human merge required.

Authorize rule kr-molit-bounded-icao@2.0.0-draft policy-sha256:13e49ee7eec3a9bfc11db72e870d028647000829954015f93175fc0661666211 scope-sha256:ca29502a69df9e8283fbdfddd0022be6988054336caacdb57f1b2076b555e413 executor-sha256:ad99fa4f9fe58b94b3fcc2c584d510df2471f716e6add8277ea6a433d27efd42. Permit bounded ICAO code candidate review only after independent physical identity admission by the exact identity rule. Recompute original AIP, NOTAM, SUP and checklist facts for the exact window. New evidence versions need fresh fact replay; mutation under an old hash rejects. No inherited v1/Indian grant, IATA, new identity creation, expanded dates, published corrections, test authority or direct main writes. Batch candidate PR only; human merge required.

New Istanbul Airport used ISL by the dated October 31 flight, before adopting IST. First ISL allocation date remains unknown; the October 29 inauguration is not used as allocation. ISL moved to Ataturk on April 6, within the day. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

ISL arrived at Ataturk in the inverse exchange with IST; preserve the existing Ataturk physical identity despite the passenger-service move. Day-only April 6 is uncertain. Current code observation supports continuity only before 2026-10-25, not future validity or a claim that passenger service continues. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Unknown original ISB allocation is bounded by the 2016 airline observation. Explicit code-transfer evidence establishes May 2018 only. Flight operations moved May 3, but no precise IATA transfer day is inferred. The old airfield remains a separate military/general-aviation site without current ISB. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

ISB transferred to a geographically separate new airport during May 2018. Every date in that month, including May 3, remains uncertain. OPIS is a distinct ICAO code, not an inherited OPRN assignment; neither ICAO allocation is added. Continuity is checked only before 2026-10-25. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Old Rostov-on-Don airport (URRR in reference data). First allocation unknown; latest start is the 2016-03-19 airline observation. ROV passed to the separate new Platov airport on 2017-11-27 per Aeroflot citing an IATA notice; the time of day is unknown, so the whole day is uncertain. The 2017-12-07 passenger transfer and the 2018-03-01 legal closure are later, separate events. An unverified fan-site claim that the code was received on 2017-11-24 is treated as a notification date and recorded in docs/curated-admissions-pr8.md. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Platov inherits ROV on 2017-11-27 (day precision), ten days before its first passengers on 2017-12-07; opening is not the code boundary. The open end is not guaranteed future validity. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Temporary code for the old airport from 2017-11-27; in use on that day for SU flights. No RVI withdrawal record was found: passenger closure on 2017-12-07 and legal closure on 2018-03-01 do not withdraw a code, so the end has no latest bound and later RVI queries remain uncertain rather than inventing a withdrawal date. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Old Yantai Laishan airport. First allocation unknown; the 2014-11-10 report observes YNT as Laishan's current code. IATA had approved YNT for Penglai and planned a coordinate update from 2014-12-11, but no implementation record was found; the latest end is the 2015-05-28 00:00 civil closure of Laishan. Every date from 2014-11-10 to 2015-05-27 is therefore uncertain; neither the planned date nor the opening is asserted as the switch. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Separate Penglai site, 57 km by road from Laishan. Start bounded by the reported IATA approval (not before the 2014-11-10 observation of YNT at Laishan) and by the complete civil transfer at 2015-05-28 00:00; current AIP and snapshot corroborate continuity. ZSYT is not admitted: no changeover record exists between the 2013 Laishan chart and the 2025 Penglai AIP. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Old Phnom Penh (Pochentong) airport. First allocation unknown; latest start is a 2008-12-31 reference-dated observation. Airline operations under PNH continued through 2025-09-08 and moved to KTI at 00:01 local on 2025-09-09. No decision to withdraw or reuse PNH was found, so the end has no latest bound; later PNH queries stay uncertain. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

First allocation unknown; latest start is the ICAO regional table dated 2014-04-25. Cambodia stated the aerodrome officially closes at 1700 UTC on 2025-09-08; aerodrome closure is not an indicator withdrawal, so the end has no latest bound. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Techo, a greenfield site separate from Pochentong and from Kratie. The IATA allocation date is unknown, so the start has no earliest bound. Schedules filed under KTI by 2025-07-22 were for travel from 2025-09-09 and show booking availability, not flights operated at Techo under KTI; they are not used as a flight-date boundary. Carriers moved operations at 00:01 local on 2025-09-09, so that whole local date stays uncertain and the latest start is 2025-09-10. KTI was previously associated with Kratie according to a Cambodian embassy notice, but no dated Kratie observation is admitted, so no Kratie assignment or reassignment boundary is asserted. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

ICAO indicator issued before operation (date unknown); published AIP operation from 0000 UTC 2025-09-04. The AIP effective date is distinct from the 2025-09-09 airline move and from any IATA date. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Actual 2013-03-29 DKR flight at Yoff bounds unknown allocation. IATA announces withdrawal for 2017-12-07 and SAA describes old DKR during that transition. Later directories retain DKR, so implementation/reinstatement is unresolved: no latest-end bound and no certified DKR interval after 2017-12-06. DKR is never assigned to Diass here; city coding is separate. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between observations, not daily direct verification or an allocation ledger.

IATA explicitly confirms DSS already assigned to Blaise Diagne on 2017-11-21; latest start is the following whole local date. Original allocation remains unknown. This pre-opening bound is administrative allocation evidence, not a booking observation, flight schedule or claim of pre-opening passenger operations. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between observations, not daily direct verification or an allocation ledger.

Actual 2013-03-29 flight observes GOOY at Yoff; current AIP retains GOOY under military administration. No ICAO withdrawal is inferred from passenger relocation or the IATA DKR notice. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between observations, not daily direct verification or an allocation ledger.

GOBD charts effective 2017-12-07 0000 UTC establish the AIP state by that local date (Dakar UTC+0), not original indicator issue. October 12 publication does not bound allocation; the start remains open to the past. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between observations, not daily direct verification or an allocation ledger.

Actual operational AAP observation on 2019-08-20 bounds latest start to 2019-08-21. May 2018 opening, October 2018 inauguration and prospective schedules are not code bounds. Earlier AAP at Andrau Airpark is outside admitted coverage; earlier dates remain uncertain. SRI withdrawal and WALS reuse are not certified. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between observations, not daily direct verification or an allocation ledger.

Observed on 2016-08-08 at the old Chaklala site; AIP AD 2 OPRN-1 dated 2021-03-25 still identifies the same runway after civil operations moved to OPIS. Coverage ends conservatively at that last observation (exclusive), not an asserted withdrawal. The fixed directory has OPRN only in gps_code, with blank icao_code; it does not extend ICAO coverage. No OPRN transfer to the new airport or new entity for military use. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

Unknown original allocation; administrative AIP designation at the new site is documented effective 2017-06-22 0001 UTC (0501 local), hence the next whole-local-date latest-start bound. Commissioning was expressly deferred to a NOTAM; this does not establish flights in 2017 or use the 2018 opening as an ICAO transfer. OPRN belongs to the separate old site. Continued OPIS is corroborated by official 2026 AIP and the unchanged fixed evidence horizon. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

Actual 2011-10-15 France-local flight record identifies departure LTBA at Ataturk. No departure time is given; a conservative additional local-day rollover yields latest start 2011-10-17. The 2026 AD 2 entry retains LTBA at Ataturk after the IATA IST/ISL exchange. Neither that passenger move nor changes in civil operations transfer LTBA to the new site. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

Unknown original allocation; SUP 04/18 documents administrative LTFM designation effective 2018-10-11, with no effective instant proved, so the conservative latest start is October 12. Its procedures and airport commissioning remained conditional on service/NOTAM; resolution before service identifies the designated site, not an operated flight. Actual LTFM departure is separately observed in the 2019-12-31 occurrence record. No ICAO transfer from LTBA or backdating from the IATA IST change is asserted. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

Actual 2016-07-08 flight identifies EDDB at Schonefeld. The existing Fluko evidence establishes Brandenburg as an extension of the same airside infrastructure; operator manual retains EDDB at Brandenburg. One continuous assignment to the existing physical ID across the 2020 SXF/BER change, T5 incorporation and T1 opening. No duplicate airport entity or invented ICAO transfer date. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

ANAC reconstructs actual 2016-04-29 UACC arrival/departure at Astana. Its log-table time standard is absent: allowing a local-day rollover at historical UTC+6 gives conservative latest start 2016-05-01. BEA confirms a local-dated 2018 landing; official 2026 AIP retains UACC on the same runway/site after TSE/NQZ. Renaming the city or airport and changing IATA code do not create another physical identity or a UACC transfer. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

User-approved certain coverage [2009-05-08, 2010-04-28). FAA 2009 airport row and scoped K-prefix rule, followed by the printed numeric issue date of NWS TIN10-18, support a reviewed continuity inference. The prior May 2010 tail is not accepted. First allocation and withdrawal remain unknown; the forecast service/closure dates are not allocation boundaries.

User-approved certain coverage [2010-05-24, 2014-07-24). Continuity is inferred between the NWS KECP association and the FAA 2014 ECP airport row under the contiguous-US K-prefix rule, with FAA replacement-site context. This is not an exact opening, initial allocation or withdrawal interval.

User-approved certain coverage [2009-05-08, 2014-07-24). Continuity is inferred between the 2009 and 2014 FAA ISN airport rows under their scoped K-prefix rules. These editions share the FAA register lineage. No 2014-2019 bridge or allocation/withdrawal date is asserted.

names.note: Canonical Russian official airport name in the original 2017 decision. Continuity from the 2006 observation to the renaming is a reviewed inference. June 21 is the first-publication effective day; whole-day resolution remains conservative because no midnight instant is established. City renames and IATA code changes do not create name intervals.

Old Yantai Laishan airport. First allocation unknown; the 2014-11-10 report observes YNT as Laishan's current code. IATA had approved YNT for Penglai and planned a coordinate update from 2014-12-11, but no implementation record was found; the latest end is the 2015-05-28 00:00 civil closure of Laishan. Every date from 2014-11-10 to 2015-05-27 is therefore uncertain; neither the planned date nor the opening is asserted as the switch. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Separate Penglai site, 57 km by road from Laishan. Start bounded by the reported IATA approval (not before the 2014-11-10 observation of YNT at Laishan) and by the complete civil transfer at 2015-05-28 00:00; current AIP and snapshot corroborate continuity. ZSYT is not admitted: no changeover record exists between the 2013 Laishan chart and the 2025 Penglai AIP. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Old Phnom Penh (Pochentong) airport. First allocation unknown; latest start is a 2008-12-31 reference-dated observation. Airline operations under PNH continued through 2025-09-08 and moved to KTI at 00:01 local on 2025-09-09. No decision to withdraw or reuse PNH was found, so the end has no latest bound; later PNH queries stay uncertain. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

First allocation unknown; latest start is the ICAO regional table dated 2014-04-25. Cambodia stated the aerodrome officially closes at 1700 UTC on 2025-09-08; aerodrome closure is not an indicator withdrawal, so the end has no latest bound. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Techo, a greenfield site separate from Pochentong and from Kratie. The IATA allocation date is unknown, so the start has no earliest bound. Schedules filed under KTI by 2025-07-22 were for travel from 2025-09-09 and show booking availability, not flights operated at Techo under KTI; they are not used as a flight-date boundary. Carriers moved operations at 00:01 local on 2025-09-09, so that whole local date stays uncertain and the latest start is 2025-09-10. KTI was previously associated with Kratie according to a Cambodian embassy notice, but no dated Kratie observation is admitted, so no Kratie assignment or reassignment boundary is asserted. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

No OPRN transfer to the new airport or new entity for military use. Unknown original allocation; administrative AIP designation at the new site is documented effective 2017-06-22 0001 UTC (0501 local), hence the next whole-local-date latest-start bound. Commissioning was expressly deferred to a NOTAM; this does not establish flights in 2017 or use the 2018 opening as an ICAO transfer. OPRN belongs to the separate old site. Continued OPIS is corroborated by official 2026 AIP and the unchanged fixed evidence horizon. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

Actual 2011-10-15 France-local flight record identifies departure LTBA at Ataturk. No departure time is given; a conservative additional local-day rollover yields latest start 2011-10-17. The 2026 AD 2 entry retains LTBA at Ataturk after the IATA IST/ISL exchange. Neither that passenger move nor changes in civil operations transfer LTBA to the new site. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

Unknown original allocation; SUP 04/18 documents administrative LTFM designation effective 2018-10-11, with no effective instant proved, so the conservative latest start is October 12. Actual LTFM departure is separately observed in the 2019-12-31 occurrence record. No ICAO transfer from LTBA or backdating from the IATA IST change is asserted. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

Actual 2016-07-08 flight identifies EDDB at Schonefeld. The existing Fluko evidence establishes Brandenburg as an extension of the same airside infrastructure; operator manual retains EDDB at Brandenburg. One continuous assignment to the existing physical ID across the 2020 SXF/BER change, T5 incorporation and T1 opening. No duplicate airport entity or invented ICAO transfer date. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

ANAC reconstructs actual 2016-04-29 UACC arrival/departure at Astana. Its log-table time standard is absent: allowing a local-day rollover at historical UTC+6 gives conservative latest start 2016-05-01. BEA confirms a local-dated 2018 landing; official 2026 AIP retains UACC on the same runway/site after TSE/NQZ. Renaming the city or airport and changing IATA code do not create another physical identity or a UACC transfer. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

IATA had approved YNT for Penglai and planned a coordinate update from 2014-12-11, but no implementation record was found; the latest end is the 2015-05-28 00:00 civil closure of Laishan. Every date from 2014-11-10 to 2015-05-27 is therefore uncertain; neither the planned date nor the opening is asserted as the switch. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Separate Penglai site, 57 km by road from Laishan. Start bounded by the reported IATA approval (not before the 2014-11-10 observation of YNT at Laishan) and by the complete civil transfer at 2015-05-28 00:00; current AIP and snapshot corroborate continuity. ZSYT is not admitted: no changeover record exists between the 2013 Laishan chart and the 2025 Penglai AIP. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Old Phnom Penh (Pochentong) airport. First allocation unknown; latest start is a 2008-12-31 reference-dated observation. Airline operations under PNH continued through 2025-09-08 and moved to KTI at 00:01 local on 2025-09-09. No decision to withdraw or reuse PNH was found, so the end has no latest bound; later PNH queries stay uncertain. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

First allocation unknown; latest start is the ICAO regional table dated 2014-04-25. Cambodia stated the aerodrome officially closes at 1700 UTC on 2025-09-08; aerodrome closure is not an indicator withdrawal, so the end has no latest bound. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Techo, a greenfield site separate from Pochentong and from Kratie. The IATA allocation date is unknown, so the start has no earliest bound. Schedules filed under KTI by 2025-07-22 were for travel from 2025-09-09 and show booking availability, not flights operated at Techo under KTI; they are not used as a flight-date boundary. Carriers moved operations at 00:01 local on 2025-09-09, so that whole local date stays uncertain and the latest start is 2025-09-10. KTI was previously associated with Kratie according to a Cambodian embassy notice, but no dated Kratie observation is admitted, so no Kratie assignment or reassignment boundary is asserted. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

ICAO indicator issued before operation (date unknown); published AIP operation from 0000 UTC 2025-09-04. The AIP effective date is distinct from the 2025-09-09 airline move and from any IATA date. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Actual 2013-03-29 DKR flight at Yoff bounds unknown allocation. IATA announces withdrawal for 2017-12-07 and SAA describes old DKR during that transition. Later directories retain DKR, so implementation/reinstatement is unresolved: no latest-end bound and no certified DKR interval after 2017-12-06. DKR is never assigned to Diass here; city coding is separate. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between observations, not daily direct verification or an allocation ledger.

IATA explicitly confirms DSS already assigned to Blaise Diagne on 2017-11-21; latest start is the following whole local date. Original allocation remains unknown. This pre-opening bound is administrative allocation evidence, not a booking observation, flight schedule or claim of pre-opening passenger operations. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between observations, not daily direct verification or an allocation ledger.

Actual 2013-03-29 flight observes GOOY at Yoff; current AIP retains GOOY under military administration. No ICAO withdrawal is inferred from passenger relocation or the IATA DKR notice. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between observations, not daily direct verification or an allocation ledger.

Actual operational AAP observation on 2019-08-20 bounds latest start to 2019-08-21. May 2018 opening, October 2018 inauguration and prospective schedules are not code bounds. Unknown original allocation; administrative AIP designation at the new site is documented effective 2017-06-22 0001 UTC (0501 local), hence the next whole-local-date latest-start bound. Commissioning was expressly deferred to a NOTAM; this does not establish flights in 2017 or use the 2018 opening as an ICAO transfer. OPRN belongs to the separate old site. Continued OPIS is corroborated by official 2026 AIP and the unchanged fixed evidence horizon. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

Actual 2011-10-15 France-local flight record identifies departure LTBA at Ataturk. No departure time is given; a conservative additional local-day rollover yields latest start 2011-10-17. The 2026 AD 2 entry retains LTBA at Ataturk after the IATA IST/ISL exchange. Neither that passenger move nor changes in civil operations transfer LTBA to the new site. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

Actual 2016-07-08 flight identifies EDDB at Schonefeld. The existing Fluko evidence establishes Brandenburg as an extension of the same airside infrastructure; operator manual retains EDDB at Brandenburg. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

Its log-table time standard is absent: allowing a local-day rollover at historical UTC+6 gives conservative latest start 2016-05-01. BEA confirms a local-dated 2018 landing; official 2026 AIP retains UACC on the same runway/site after TSE/NQZ. approval.body: Authorize rule official-aip-stable-physical-identity@0.1.0-draft policy-sha256:7eadcab59d93a2f33c9e9237ad2dc2e258e129f4995bbf60cba35c26d6fe65ae scope-sha256:597ddbc5afeb66df29bf7dcb405846e9ac912ae4bfa93bfd2b71c24a6c8b4e65 executor-sha256:ad99fa4f9fe58b94b3fcc2c584d510df2471f716e6add8277ea6a433d27efd42. Permit automatic physical-site UUID allocation for all future qualifying low-risk airports in this country/issuer scope, without per-airport approval. Require original replay, independent operator site/address evidence, complete edition and competition checks. No code/name validity, relocation, correction, test authority, or direct main writes. Candidate PR only; human merge required.

Authorize rule kr-molit-bounded-icao@2.0.0-draft policy-sha256:13e49ee7eec3a9bfc11db72e870d028647000829954015f93175fc0661666211 scope-sha256:ca29502a69df9e8283fbdfddd0022be6988054336caacdb57f1b2076b555e413 executor-sha256:ad99fa4f9fe58b94b3fcc2c584d510df2471f716e6add8277ea6a433d27efd42. Permit bounded ICAO code candidate review only after independent physical identity admission by the exact identity rule. Recompute original AIP, NOTAM, SUP and checklist facts for the exact window. New evidence versions need fresh fact replay; mutation under an old hash rejects. No inherited v1/Indian grant, IATA, new identity creation, expanded dates, published corrections, test authority or direct main writes. Batch candidate PR only; human merge required.

No RVI withdrawal record was found: passenger closure on 2017-12-07 and legal closure on 2018-03-01 do not withdraw a code, so the end has no latest bound and later RVI queries remain uncertain rather than inventing a withdrawal date. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Old Yantai Laishan airport. First allocation unknown; the 2014-11-10 report observes YNT as Laishan's current code. IATA had approved YNT for Penglai and planned a coordinate update from 2014-12-11, but no implementation record was found; the latest end is the 2015-05-28 00:00 civil closure of Laishan. Every date from 2014-11-10 to 2015-05-27 is therefore uncertain; neither the planned date nor the opening is asserted as the switch. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Separate Penglai site, 57 km by road from Laishan. Start bounded by the reported IATA approval (not before the 2014-11-10 observation of YNT at Laishan) and by the complete civil transfer at 2015-05-28 00:00; current AIP and snapshot corroborate continuity. ZSYT is not admitted: no changeover record exists between the 2013 Laishan chart and the 2025 Penglai AIP. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Old Phnom Penh (Pochentong) airport. First allocation unknown; latest start is a 2008-12-31 reference-dated observation. Airline operations under PNH continued through 2025-09-08 and moved to KTI at 00:01 local on 2025-09-09. No decision to withdraw or reuse PNH was found, so the end has no latest bound; later PNH queries stay uncertain. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

First allocation unknown; latest start is the ICAO regional table dated 2014-04-25. Cambodia stated the aerodrome officially closes at 1700 UTC on 2025-09-08; aerodrome closure is not an indicator withdrawal, so the end has no latest bound. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Techo, a greenfield site separate from Pochentong and from Kratie. The IATA allocation date is unknown, so the start has no earliest bound. Schedules filed under KTI by 2025-07-22 were for travel from 2025-09-09 and show booking availability, not flights operated at Techo under KTI; they are not used as a flight-date boundary. Carriers moved operations at 00:01 local on 2025-09-09, so that whole local date stays uncertain and the latest start is 2025-09-10. KTI was previously associated with Kratie according to a Cambodian embassy notice, but no dated Kratie observation is admitted, so no Kratie assignment or reassignment boundary is asserted. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

ICAO indicator issued before operation (date unknown); published AIP operation from 0000 UTC 2025-09-04. The AIP effective date is distinct from the 2025-09-09 airline move and from any IATA date. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Actual 2013-03-29 DKR flight at Yoff bounds unknown allocation. IATA announces withdrawal for 2017-12-07 and SAA describes old DKR during that transition. DKR is never assigned to Diass here; city coding is separate. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between observations, not daily direct verification or an allocation ledger.

Observed on 2016-08-08 at the old Chaklala site; AIP AD 2 OPRN-1 dated 2021-03-25 still identifies the same runway after civil operations moved to OPIS. No OPRN transfer to the new airport or new entity for military use. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

Unknown original allocation; administrative AIP designation at the new site is documented effective 2017-06-22 0001 UTC (0501 local), hence the next whole-local-date latest-start bound. Commissioning was expressly deferred to a NOTAM; this does not establish flights in 2017 or use the 2018 opening as an ICAO transfer. OPRN belongs to the separate old site. Continued OPIS is corroborated by official 2026 AIP and the unchanged fixed evidence horizon. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

Actual 2011-10-15 France-local flight record identifies departure LTBA at Ataturk. No departure time is given; a conservative additional local-day rollover yields latest start 2011-10-17. The 2026 AD 2 entry retains LTBA at Ataturk after the IATA IST/ISL exchange. Neither that passenger move nor changes in civil operations transfer LTBA to the new site. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

Unknown original allocation; SUP 04/18 documents administrative LTFM designation effective 2018-10-11, with no effective instant proved, so the conservative latest start is October 12. Its procedures and airport commissioning remained conditional on service/NOTAM; resolution before service identifies the designated site, not an operated flight. Actual LTFM departure is separately observed in the 2019-12-31 occurrence record. No ICAO transfer from LTBA or backdating from the IATA IST change is asserted. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

Actual 2016-07-08 flight identifies EDDB at Schonefeld. The existing Fluko evidence establishes Brandenburg as an extension of the same airside infrastructure; operator manual retains EDDB at Brandenburg. One continuous assignment to the existing physical ID across the 2020 SXF/BER change, T5 incorporation and T1 opening. No duplicate airport entity or invented ICAO transfer date. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

ANAC reconstructs actual 2016-04-29 UACC arrival/departure at Astana. Its log-table time standard is absent: allowing a local-day rollover at historical UTC+6 gives conservative latest start 2016-05-01. BEA confirms a local-dated 2018 landing; official 2026 AIP retains UACC on the same runway/site after TSE/NQZ. Renaming the city or airport and changing IATA code do not create another physical identity or a UACC transfer. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

Old Yantai Laishan airport. First allocation unknown; the 2014-11-10 report observes YNT as Laishan's current code. IATA had approved YNT for Penglai and planned a coordinate update from 2014-12-11, but no implementation record was found; the latest end is the 2015-05-28 00:00 civil closure of Laishan. Every date from 2014-11-10 to 2015-05-27 is therefore uncertain; neither the planned date nor the opening is asserted as the switch. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Separate Penglai site, 57 km by road from Laishan. Start bounded by the reported IATA approval (not before the 2014-11-10 observation of YNT at Laishan) and by the complete civil transfer at 2015-05-28 00:00; current AIP and snapshot corroborate continuity. ZSYT is not admitted: no changeover record exists between the 2013 Laishan chart and the 2025 Penglai AIP. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Airline operations under PNH continued through 2025-09-08 and moved to KTI at 00:01 local on 2025-09-09. No decision to withdraw or reuse PNH was found, so the end has no latest bound; later PNH queries stay uncertain. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Techo, a greenfield site separate from Pochentong and from Kratie. The IATA allocation date is unknown, so the start has no earliest bound. Schedules filed under KTI by 2025-07-22 were for travel from 2025-09-09 and show booking availability, not flights operated at Techo under KTI; they are not used as a flight-date boundary. Carriers moved operations at 00:01 local on 2025-09-09, so that whole local date stays uncertain and the latest start is 2025-09-10. KTI was previously associated with Kratie according to a Cambodian embassy notice, but no dated Kratie observation is admitted, so no Kratie assignment or reassignment boundary is asserted. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Actual 2013-03-29 flight observes GOOY at Yoff; current AIP retains GOOY under military administration. No ICAO withdrawal is inferred from passenger relocation or the IATA DKR notice. Earlier AAP at Andrau Airpark is outside admitted coverage; earlier dates remain uncertain. SRI withdrawal and WALS reuse are not certified. No OPRN transfer to the new airport or new entity for military use. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

Unknown original allocation; administrative AIP designation at the new site is documented effective 2017-06-22 0001 UTC (0501 local), hence the next whole-local-date latest-start bound. Commissioning was expressly deferred to a NOTAM; this does not establish flights in 2017 or use the 2018 opening as an ICAO transfer. OPRN belongs to the separate old site. Continued OPIS is corroborated by official 2026 AIP and the unchanged fixed evidence horizon. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

Actual 2011-10-15 France-local flight record identifies departure LTBA at Ataturk. No departure time is given; a conservative additional local-day rollover yields latest start 2011-10-17. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

Actual 2016-07-08 flight identifies EDDB at Schonefeld. The existing Fluko evidence establishes Brandenburg as an extension of the same airside infrastructure; operator manual retains EDDB at Brandenburg. One continuous assignment to the existing physical ID across the 2020 SXF/BER change, T5 incorporation and T1 opening. No duplicate airport entity or invented ICAO transfer date. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

Its log-table time standard is absent: allowing a local-day rollover at historical UTC+6 gives conservative latest start 2016-05-01. New Istanbul Airport used ISL by the dated October 31 flight, before adopting IST. First ISL allocation date remains unknown; the October 29 inauguration is not used as allocation. ISL moved to Ataturk on April 6, within the day. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

ISL arrived at Ataturk in the inverse exchange with IST; preserve the existing Ataturk physical identity despite the passenger-service move. Day-only April 6 is uncertain. Current code observation supports continuity only before 2026-10-25, not future validity or a claim that passenger service continues. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Unknown original ISB allocation is bounded by the 2016 airline observation. Explicit code-transfer evidence establishes May 2018 only. Flight operations moved May 3, but no precise IATA transfer day is inferred. The old airfield remains a separate military/general-aviation site without current ISB. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

ISB transferred to a geographically separate new airport during May 2018. Every date in that month, including May 3, remains uncertain. OPIS is a distinct ICAO code, not an inherited OPRN assignment; neither ICAO allocation is added. Continuity is checked only before 2026-10-25. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

First allocation remains unknown; latest start is only a dated observation bound. The continuing Schonefeld airfield expanded into Brandenburg; old facilities became T5. October 25 airport-code change is separate from October 31 T1 opening. Pre-2020 BER metropolitan/city-code use is outside the airport namespace; no airport assignment is created for it. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

The open end does not guarantee validity on or after 2026-10-25. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Old Rostov-on-Don airport (URRR in reference data). First allocation unknown; latest start is the 2016-03-19 airline observation. ROV passed to the separate new Platov airport on 2017-11-27 per Aeroflot citing an IATA notice; the time of day is unknown, so the whole day is uncertain. The 2017-12-07 passenger transfer and the 2018-03-01 legal closure are later, separate events. An unverified fan-site claim that the code was received on 2017-11-24 is treated as a notification date and recorded in docs/curated-admissions-pr8.md. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Platov inherits ROV on 2017-11-27 (day precision), ten days before its first passengers on 2017-12-07; opening is not the code boundary. The open end is not guaranteed future validity. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Temporary code for the old airport from 2017-11-27; in use on that day for SU flights. No RVI withdrawal record was found: passenger closure on 2017-12-07 and legal closure on 2018-03-01 do not withdraw a code, so the end has no latest bound and later RVI queries remain uncertain rather than inventing a withdrawal date. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Old Yantai Laishan airport. First allocation unknown; the 2014-11-10 report observes YNT as Laishan's current code. IATA had approved YNT for Penglai and planned a coordinate update from 2014-12-11, but no implementation record was found; the latest end is the 2015-05-28 00:00 civil closure of Laishan. Every date from 2014-11-10 to 2015-05-27 is therefore uncertain; neither the planned date nor the opening is asserted as the switch. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Separate Penglai site, 57 km by road from Laishan. Start bounded by the reported IATA approval (not before the 2014-11-10 observation of YNT at Laishan) and by the complete civil transfer at 2015-05-28 00:00; current AIP and snapshot corroborate continuity. ZSYT is not admitted: no changeover record exists between the 2013 Laishan chart and the 2025 Penglai AIP. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Old Phnom Penh (Pochentong) airport. First allocation unknown; latest start is a 2008-12-31 reference-dated observation. Airline operations under PNH continued through 2025-09-08 and moved to KTI at 00:01 local on 2025-09-09. No decision to withdraw or reuse PNH was found, so the end has no latest bound; later PNH queries stay uncertain. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

First allocation unknown; latest start is the ICAO regional table dated 2014-04-25. Cambodia stated the aerodrome officially closes at 1700 UTC on 2025-09-08; aerodrome closure is not an indicator withdrawal, so the end has no latest bound. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Techo, a greenfield site separate from Pochentong and from Kratie. The IATA allocation date is unknown, so the start has no earliest bound. Schedules filed under KTI by 2025-07-22 were for travel from 2025-09-09 and show booking availability, not flights operated at Techo under KTI; they are not used as a flight-date boundary. Carriers moved operations at 00:01 local on 2025-09-09, so that whole local date stays uncertain and the latest start is 2025-09-10. KTI was previously associated with Kratie according to a Cambodian embassy notice, but no dated Kratie observation is admitted, so no Kratie assignment or reassignment boundary is asserted. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

ICAO indicator issued before operation (date unknown); published AIP operation from 0000 UTC 2025-09-04. The AIP effective date is distinct from the 2025-09-09 airline move and from any IATA date. The continuous interval between observations is a reviewed continuity inference, not an official allocation ledger or daily verification.

Actual 2013-03-29 DKR flight at Yoff bounds unknown allocation. IATA announces withdrawal for 2017-12-07 and SAA describes old DKR during that transition. Later directories retain DKR, so implementation/reinstatement is unresolved: no latest-end bound and no certified DKR interval after 2017-12-06. DKR is never assigned to Diass here; city coding is separate. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between observations, not daily direct verification or an allocation ledger.

IATA explicitly confirms DSS already assigned to Blaise Diagne on 2017-11-21; latest start is the following whole local date. Original allocation remains unknown. This pre-opening bound is administrative allocation evidence, not a booking observation, flight schedule or claim of pre-opening passenger operations. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between observations, not daily direct verification or an allocation ledger.

Actual 2013-03-29 flight observes GOOY at Yoff; current AIP retains GOOY under military administration. No ICAO withdrawal is inferred from passenger relocation or the IATA DKR notice. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between observations, not daily direct verification or an allocation ledger.

GOBD charts effective 2017-12-07 0000 UTC establish the AIP state by that local date (Dakar UTC+0), not original indicator issue. October 12 publication does not bound allocation; the start remains open to the past. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between observations, not daily direct verification or an allocation ledger.

Actual operational AAP observation on 2019-08-20 bounds latest start to 2019-08-21. May 2018 opening, October 2018 inauguration and prospective schedules are not code bounds. Earlier AAP at Andrau Airpark is outside admitted coverage; earlier dates remain uncertain. SRI withdrawal and WALS reuse are not certified. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between observations, not daily direct verification or an allocation ledger.

Observed on 2016-08-08 at the old Chaklala site; AIP AD 2 OPRN-1 dated 2021-03-25 still identifies the same runway after civil operations moved to OPIS. Coverage ends conservatively at that last observation (exclusive), not an asserted withdrawal. The fixed directory has OPRN only in gps_code, with blank icao_code; it does not extend ICAO coverage. No OPRN transfer to the new airport or new entity for military use. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

Unknown original allocation; administrative AIP designation at the new site is documented effective 2017-06-22 0001 UTC (0501 local), hence the next whole-local-date latest-start bound. Commissioning was expressly deferred to a NOTAM; this does not establish flights in 2017 or use the 2018 opening as an ICAO transfer. OPRN belongs to the separate old site. Continued OPIS is corroborated by official 2026 AIP and the unchanged fixed evidence horizon. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

Actual 2011-10-15 France-local flight record identifies departure LTBA at Ataturk. No departure time is given; a conservative additional local-day rollover yields latest start 2011-10-17. The 2026 AD 2 entry retains LTBA at Ataturk after the IATA IST/ISL exchange. Neither that passenger move nor changes in civil operations transfer LTBA to the new site. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

Unknown original allocation; SUP 04/18 documents administrative LTFM designation effective 2018-10-11, with no effective instant proved, so the conservative latest start is October 12. Its procedures and airport commissioning remained conditional on service/NOTAM; resolution before service identifies the designated site, not an operated flight. Actual LTFM departure is separately observed in the 2019-12-31 occurrence record. No ICAO transfer from LTBA or backdating from the IATA IST change is asserted. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

Actual 2016-07-08 flight identifies EDDB at Schonefeld. The existing Fluko evidence establishes Brandenburg as an extension of the same airside infrastructure; operator manual retains EDDB at Brandenburg. One continuous assignment to the existing physical ID across the 2020 SXF/BER change, T5 incorporation and T1 opening. No duplicate airport entity or invented ICAO transfer date. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

ANAC reconstructs actual 2016-04-29 UACC arrival/departure at Astana. Its log-table time standard is absent: allowing a local-day rollover at historical UTC+6 gives conservative latest start 2016-05-01. BEA confirms a local-dated 2018 landing; official 2026 AIP retains UACC on the same runway/site after TSE/NQZ. Renaming the city or airport and changing IATA code do not create another physical identity or a UACC transfer. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference between dated observations, not daily direct verification, a first-allocation date, or proof that flights operated on every resolved date.

User-approved certain coverage [2009-05-08, 2010-04-28). FAA 2009 airport row and scoped K-prefix rule, followed by the printed numeric issue date of NWS TIN10-18, support a reviewed continuity inference. The prior May 2010 tail is not accepted. First allocation and withdrawal remain unknown; the forecast service/closure dates are not allocation boundaries.

User-approved certain coverage [2010-05-24, 2014-07-24). Continuity is inferred between the NWS KECP association and the FAA 2014 ECP airport row under the contiguous-US K-prefix rule, with FAA replacement-site context. This is not an exact opening, initial allocation or withdrawal interval.

User-approved certain coverage [2009-05-08, 2014-07-24). Continuity is inferred between the 2009 and 2014 FAA ISN airport rows under their scoped K-prefix rules. These editions share the FAA register lineage. No 2014-2019 bridge or allocation/withdrawal date is asserted.

names.note: Canonical Russian official airport name in the original 2017 decision. Continuity from the 2006 observation to the renaming is a reviewed inference. Original naming date remains unknown; dates before 2006-11-21 are uncertain. June 21 is the first-publication effective day; whole-day resolution remains conservative because no midnight instant is established. City renames and IATA code changes do not create name intervals.

names.name: Международный аэропорт Нурсултан Назарбаев
names.note: Canonical Russian official airport name from the original renaming, with later aviation-administration use and the fixed current-directory label corroborating continuation. The whole interval is a reviewed continuity inference, not direct evidence for every day. Known effective day is 2017-06-21, not signing day 2017-06-20 or the 2020 IATA code change.
